evidence: X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) was utilized to identify the surface composition of Cu2S films before and after exposure to air. Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) analysis of films grown at 80 /C14 C reveals smaller grains consistent with a non-oriented polycrystalline film. X-ray Diffraction (XRD) was carried out in q–2q mode on samples deposited on quartz. Ellipsometry was used to deduce approximate optical constants from variable angle spectroscopy. Hall measurements were acquired on an Ecopia HMS-3000 Hall Measurement System. Film thicknesses were deduced from spectroscopic ellipsometry. X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) was performed in a custom-built instrument equipped with a hemispherical electron energy analyzer.
